abstract.t:
AI agents are becoming some of the biggest users of the Internet. A site today has no neutral way to tell a good agent from a bot. The site sees either an anonymous request it cannot trust, or a request carrying a long-lived credential it cannot check. The result is blunt blocking on one side and unchecked abuse on the other.
This document defines the SwarmSpeak Handshake, a protocol that lets an AI agent present a short-lived, narrowly scoped, signed statement of who it acts for and what it is allowed to do, and lets a site verify that statement cheaply before serving the request. The agent proves authority with a principal-signed capability certificate, a short-lived directory-signed status proof, and an HTTP Message Signature. The site sees only a per-origin pseudonym for the agent, never a global tracking identifier. Every completed session at a handshake-accepting site produces an itemized receipt, and receipted sessions are recorded in an append-only audit log.
This is an individual submission. It is not a product of any IETF working group, it has not been reviewed by any IETF working group, and it does not represent IETF consensus. It is published to invite review and to record prior art for the shapes defined here: the capability certificate, the per-origin certificate view, the short-lived status proof, and the receipt.
